comments.author: brandonb
comments.story: Poorly Managed HealthCare.gov Construction Cost $840M, Watchdog Finds
comments.text: I was part of the "tech surge" brought in to help patch up healthcare.gov in December. The GAO report gives a decent idea of what went wrong in 2010-2013 from a high-level contracting and policy perspective, but it doesn't really give much technical detail or describe what was broken about the organization, software architecture, and culture. A couple of my colleagues have given talks on healthcare.gov from the perspective of the engineers who worked around the clock to help get the site running again: [LINK] [VIDEO] A small team is also re-writing the site, starting with the most troublesome components for the next open enrollment period. Wired covered some of what is going on here: [LINK] If any of you out there want to help, please email jobs@hcgov.us!

comments.text: Worth watching: [VIDEO] I like the way the presenter sums it up...it seems like each contractor was responsible for their own little piece of the stack, and nobody was actually responsible for delivering a website . That should've been the gating criteria.
